_what: Weight A/Bs for .github/workflows/experiments.yml. One entry per arm; every entry runs as its own job, in parallel, on its own runner.

_schema.slug: filename-safe id; names the artifact and the report
_schema.held: the held-out sample, disjoint from seeds -- required, because --decide is gated on a held sample existing and passing --decide alone does nothing
_schema.title: one line for the generated note
_schema.context: why this arm, what it should show, and what it cannot -- the runner will not interpret the result for you

_sizing: 128 seeds by default and 256 the ceiling, matching scripts/lib/queue_common.sh. The reason for 128 is early stopping: ACCEPTANCE min_games is 150 pooled, so an 80-seed run is 160 games and --decide has ten games of slack. Measured 2026-09-12: an 80-seed run saved 4%, a 128-seed run 16%. The reason for 256 as a ceiling is that half-width falls as 1/sqrt(n) and 512 would buy +/-0.028 for four and a half hours.
_burst: The local queue existed because one machine runs one thing at a time; a runner per arm removes that. Prefer MORE ARMS AT FULL SIZE over fewer underpowered ones -- several 2026-09-12 experiments read +/-0.06 to +/-0.075 and could not settle what they were asked, purely because the box was the constraint.

experiments.title: region at par (1.0 vs 1.3), full-size re-run on current main
experiments.context: Rebuild step 2 prices factor-1 value with region at par (2026-09-14-value-rebuild-plan). The 2026-09-14 arm read pooled ~0.514 (0.523 over 128 seeds, 0.496 over 64 held) on the superseded pre-merge model: a lean, not a verdict. Re-run at full 128+64 on current main (italy default, rival urgency, retention merged). Shows whether par is free; cannot ship calibration by itself, the rebuild re-derives factor 1 anyway.

experiments.title: contested reach at zero (0.0 vs 0.25), isolated on current main
experiments.context: Isolates the contested-zero piece of the removals bundle without the five-bucket change. The 2026-09-14 arm read pooled 0.512 (0.498 over 128, 0.539 over 64 held) pre-italy: dead heat leaning up. Re-run on the stronger base; informs the five-bucket bisect whichever way it lands. Measures only the weight piece: the flat holding bonus is code, not a weight, and is not covered by this arm.

experiments.title: no coup discount (1.0 vs 0.9), isolated ablation at full size
experiments.context: The 2026-09-09 audit proposed testing coup_discount=1 as an isolated ablation; the 2026-09-12 arms came back not-measurably-worse at +/-0.06 to +/-0.075, too wide to act on. Full 128+64 re-run on current main. A pass means the discount is free, not that it is useless; a fail prices the discount. Cannot distinguish a useless discount from coups mispriced elsewhere.

experiments.title: reach value halved (0.75 vs 1.5), first reading
experiments.context: access scales all reach-into-battlegrounds value and ships at an uncalibrated 1.5 (provenance: underdetermined, no note). First reading at half: a pass means the reach term can shrink and the next bisect quarters it; a fail means 1.5 is load-bearing. Cannot say where in (0.75, 1.5] the edge is, only which side of 0.75 it is on.

experiments.title: control value halved (0.75 vs 1.5), first reading
experiments.context: control values a battleground's control for the access term; expert reasoning puts a 1-stability non-battleground at 1.25-1.67 per Op, but the region model it belongs to is measured wrong overall so it inherits that doubt. First reading at half on current main. A pass shrinks it toward the rebuild's factor-1 replacement; a fail keeps 1.5 until the rebuild. Cannot validate the expert reasoning itself, only the scale.

experiments.title: battleground margin credit halved (0.125 vs 0.25), first reading
experiments.context: margin_battleground gives partial tier-flip credit per battleground of margin, fitted to expert valuations (31 -> 26 misses). First reading at half: tests whether the fitted credit survives contact with self-play strength. A pass reopens the fit; a fail keeps it. Cannot distinguish a wrong scale from a wrong shape (the rebuild computes this per future scoring turn).

experiments.title: country margin credit halved (0.025 vs 0.05), first reading
experiments.context: margin_country is the per-country counterpart of margin_bg, same expert fit. Same read as its sibling arm: a pass reopens the fit, a fail keeps 0.05. Run as a separate arm rather than bundled so a rejection attributes to one credit, not the pair.

experiments.title: presence-progress weight halved (1.4 vs 2.8), first reading
experiments.context: progress scales credit toward a first controlled country where a side has none (e.g. USSR Iraq); ships at an uncalibrated 2.8. First reading at half on current main. A pass means presence races are over-weighted and quarters come next; a fail means the urgency is real. Cannot see the positions the credit is for (early presence fights are rare in the sample), same caveat as no-f5.

experiments.title: rival-held urgency halved (0.5 vs 1.0), first reading
experiments.context: scoring_rival just shipped with deck-tracking (ACCEPTED 0.520) at 1.0 on no basis beyond symmetry with the holding bonus; 0.0 is off. This arm bisects [0, 1]: a pass says urgency can shrink and 0.25 comes next; a fail says the symmetry guess holds. Cannot price the deck model's p_opponent_holds itself, only this weight on it.
